title: Console Trajectory Hyperrail: consolidated lane model for nav, rollouts & cost lenses
creator: Maya Chen
description: Summary: Propose a new top-to-bottom information architecture pattern we call the 'Trajectory Hyperrail' to unify navigation for routes (apps, dashboards), workspace switching, rollout management and cost lenses. The Hyperrail is a compact, adaptive rail that surfaces route-level controls (rollout canaries, cost breakdown toggles, metric lenses) without forcing users into a separate product surface. This ticket captures the design spec, prototype variants, acceptance criteria, engineering constraints and the current review notes.
background: Current console navigation fragments cause frequent context switching: rollouts live under Projects -> Rollouts, cost analysis under Billing -> Cost Explorer, and workspace switching requires a modal overlay. This fragmentation increases time-to-insight for platform teams who need to correlate model route changes with cost regressions and rollout health. Research (interviews with 12 internal and 6 pilot customers) showed a 32% increase in task time when users had to open multiple surfaces to diagnose a rollout-related cost spike.
goals:
1) Reduce cross-surface navigation for common operational workflows (diagnose rollout -> adjust canary -> check cost delta)
2) Surface per-route cost and rollout controls inline without increasing cognitive load
3) Keep primary left rail compact for small screens while enabling rich contextual panels on wider viewports
4) Provide a migration path for existing power-user workflows and keyboard-first interactions
constraints:
- Must reuse existing Console routing primitives (no backend rewrites for route IDs)
- Minimal additional API surface: use existing modelRoute metadata for rollout & billing annotations
- Performance SLO: new rail must not add >40ms to route load time
- Accessibility: keyboard navigation and screen-reader labels required
- Backwards compatibility for custom navigation driven by admin settings
proposed_solution:
Trajectory Hyperrail concept: a single collapsible rail with three semantic lanes (Primary Routes, Workspace Lanes, and Lenses).
- Primary Routes lane: canonical product sections (Overview, Models, Deployments, Billing). Persistent icons + progressive disclosure on hover or focus.
- Workspace Lanes: horizontally stacked workspace chips that support fast switch, hover previews (micro-summaries), and a lightweight dropdown for workspace actions.
- Lenses lane: contextual toggles that activate route-level overlays: Rollout Lens (canary controls, percent sliders, rollback), Cost Lens (token and GPU breakdown, 7/30/90 day deltas), Observability Lens (traces/errors). Lenses appear as micro-controls tied to the active route and are persisted in URL as query params for shareability.
Variants explored in prototype set: 'Overlay-first' (rail triggers a full-width overlay for lens detail), 'Inline-panel' (lens expands to a middle pane between rail and content), and 'Micro-pop' (compact popover with deep-link to full dashboards).
acceptance_criteria: Primary navigation unchanged for users who collapse the rail
Workspace switching <= 1 additional click from current baseline
Rollout Lens allows canary adjustments and commits without navigating away from active route
Cost Lens surfaces per-route 7/30/90 day token & infra deltas and links to full Cost Explorer
Keyboard navigation flows for hyperrail validated in accessibility QA
